variations.name: Mass timber manufacturing (CLT, glulam, DLT/NLT)
variations.description: Factories laminate dimensional lumber into large structural panels and beams (CLT, glulam, DLT/NLT) that replace much of a building's concrete and steel frame while storing biogenic carbon in the structure for decades.

companies.name: Stora Enso
companies.what: One of the world's largest CLT/LVL producers, with mills across Europe and the Sylva prefabricated mass-timber kit-of-parts building system.
companies.signal: ~EUR 9B-revenue forest products group; multiple dedicated CLT mills; mature European market leader

companies.name: Binderholz
companies.what: Family-owned Austrian group that is among the world's largest integrated solid-wood processors, producing CLT and glulam at scale with US capacity via the Klausner mill acquisitions.
companies.signal: 60+ sites across Europe and US; among largest global sawmill/CLT groups

companies.name: KLH Massivholz
companies.what: Austrian CLT pioneer producing cross-laminated timber since 1999 and exporting panels worldwide.
companies.signal: 25+ years of CLT production; one of the original European CLT brands

companies.name: Mercer Mass Timber
companies.what: Largest North American mass-timber producer after buying Structurlam's plants; runs one of the world's largest CLT presses in Spokane Valley, WA plus glulam capacity.
companies.signal: Acquired Structurlam assets for ~$81M (2023); ~45,000 m3 glulam plus large-format CLT capacity

companies.name: Structurlam
companies.what: Pioneer North American CLT/glulam maker (founded 1962, CLT since 2011) that supplied landmark projects like Brock Commons before collapsing.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 in April 2023 after losing the Walmart HQ contract; BC and Arkansas plants sold to Mercer International for ~$81M

companies.name: SmartLam North America
companies.what: First US CLT manufacturer (2016, Montana), now with a second campus in Dothan, Alabama and a glulam line being added.
companies.signal: ~$62M glulam facility addition in Dothan, AL; plants in MT and AL

companies.name: Sterling Structural
companies.what: Cost-focused Midwest/Texas CLT producer that entered via CLT access mats and now makes building-grade CLT and mass timber components.
companies.signal: Plants in Phoenix, IL and Lufkin, TX; largest US producer of CLT industrial matting

companies.name: Element5
companies.what: Ontario CLT/glulam manufacturer with one of Canada's most automated plants in St. Thomas.
companies.signal: Doubled capacity to 100,000 m3/yr with new glulam line (Sept 2025); $107M expansion; Hasslacher Norica Timber became majority shareholder

companies.name: Freres Engineered Wood
companies.what: Oregon family mill (1922) that invented the Mass Plywood Panel (MPP), a veneer-based alternative to CLT used in the Portland airport's mass timber roof.
companies.signal: MPP commercially shipping; supplied PDX terminal roof, one of the largest US mass timber projects

variations.name: Mass timber design-build, fabricators and developers
variations.description: Specialist fabricators, engineer-builders and developers take mass timber from mill to erected frame — design, CNC fabrication, logistics and installation — which is the bottleneck step for delivering timber buildings at conventional cost and schedule.

companies.name: Timberlab
companies.what: Swinerton's full-service mass timber company spanning engineering, fabrication and install, now vertically integrating into manufacturing.
companies.signal: Acquired American Laminators glulam plants (2024); building one of the largest US CLT plants (Millersburg, OR; 7-9M sq ft/yr; completion early 2027)

companies.name: intelligent City
companies.what: Vancouver company using robotic prefabrication to produce a standardized mass-timber building platform for mid- and high-rise housing.
companies.signal: Venture-backed (Series A 2021); automated panel factory in Delta, BC; multiple Canadian mass-timber housing projects

companies.name: StructureCraft
companies.what: Engineer-led timber builder that developed modern dowel-laminated timber (DLT) and runs a purpose-built DLT plant in Abbotsford, BC.
companies.signal: Delivered structures for T3 Minneapolis and 100+ major timber projects

companies.name: Seagate Mass Timber
companies.what: One of North America's largest dedicated mass-timber fabrication and installation contractors, working across BC and the US.
companies.signal: Decades of heavy-timber erection experience; active on large commercial mass timber projects

companies.name: Nordic Structures
companies.what: Vertically integrated Québec producer (Chantiers Chibougamau) combining black-spruce CLT/glulam manufacturing with in-house engineering and project delivery.
companies.signal: Supplied the 13-storey Origine tower in Québec City, an early tall-timber landmark

companies.name: Hines (T3)
companies.what: Global developer with the repeatable T3 (Timber, Transit, Technology) heavy-timber office product line, the largest institutional mass-timber development program.
companies.signal: Dozens of T3 buildings delivered or underway globally since T3 Minneapolis (2016)

companies.name: Juno
companies.what: Productized plug-and-play mass-timber apartment system; delivered the first fully component-based mass timber building in the US (24-unit East Austin project).
companies.signal: Raised ~$50M (Series A $20M, 2021, Comcast Ventures); founder/CEO departed to project44 in March 2025 with little public company activity since

variations.name: Engineered bamboo and fast-growing-fiber structural products
variations.description: Bamboo and other fast-growing grasses are laminated or pressed into structural studs, beams and wall panels that match timber strength while regrowing in 3-5 years and sequestering carbon faster per acre than trees.

companies.name: BamCore
companies.what: Hollow-core bamboo-hybrid panelized wall system (Prime Wall) that replaces stud framing in low-rise housing with higher insulation and lower carbon.
companies.signal: Series B raised May 2024; Tracxn reports ~$142M cumulative funding across 10 rounds; selected for a federal low-carbon building materials grant (Jul 2024)

companies.name: Rizome
companies.what: Grows giant bamboo in the Philippines and Florida and manufactures engineered bamboo lumber, building the supply chain end to end.
companies.signal: $100M engineered-bamboo facility in Cagayan de Oro; won 2024 US Secretary of State's Award for Corporate Excellence (Climate Resilience)

companies.name: ReNuTeq
companies.what: St. Louis maker of structural engineered bamboo (SEB) glulam-style frames and components, fire-tested for commercial projects.
companies.signal: Commercial installs including the Danforth Plant Science Center Farm Pavilion (2024)

companies.name: MOSO International
companies.what: Dutch market leader in industrial bamboo products (beams, panels, decking, cladding) with global distribution, mostly semi-structural applications.
companies.signal: 25+ years in bamboo products; distribution across 50+ countries

variations.white_space: Almost no code-approved structural bamboo exists in Western markets: the fiber supply sits in the tropics, ICC/Eurocode certification is slow and expensive, and lamination plants are capital-intensive. The opening is code-certified bamboo studs/panels produced near equatorial fiber with US production-builder distribution, sold on hurricane and fire performance plus carbon — the path BamCore's builder partnerships and Rizome's $100M plant are testing.

variations.name: Carbon-storing and bio-based boards, blocks and finishes
variations.description: Agricultural fibers (grass, straw, hemp) and recycled cellulose are pressed into drop-in replacements for OSB, drywall and masonry blocks, storing biogenic carbon in walls instead of emitting it from gypsum, cement and clear-cut timber.

companies.name: Plantd
companies.what: North Carolina startup making carbon-negative structural sheathing panels from fast-growing perennial grass on all-electric production lines.
companies.signal: Raised $22M (Mar 2026) on top of ~$20.6M prior; multi-year D.R. Horton contract for 10 million panels (~90,000 homes)

companies.name: Adaptavate
companies.what: UK developer of Breathaboard, a compostable carbon-sequestering plasterboard alternative made on the world's first continuous bio-board pilot line.
companies.signal: GBP 2.7M pre-Series A (Apr 2025) plus Innovate UK grants; industrial demonstrator ('Project Crystal') next; saves ~4 kgCO2/m2 vs gypsum board

companies.name: IsoHemp
companies.what: Belgian manufacturer of hempcrete masonry blocks with an automated plant, the European volume leader for hemp-lime construction.
companies.signal: Factory capacity ~5M blocks/yr; thousands of projects across Europe

companies.name: JustBioFiber
companies.what: Alberta maker of interlocking Lego-style structural hempcrete blocks with an integrated load-bearing frame.
companies.signal: Built the zero-carbon Trent University forensics building; pandemic-era financial struggles reported (2024) and little recent commercial activity visible

companies.name: Ecococon
companies.what: Lithuanian manufacturer of prefabricated straw-insulated structural wall panels, Passive House Institute certified, shipped across Europe and North America.
companies.signal: PHI-certified component; hundreds of buildings delivered across 20+ countries

companies.name: HempWood (Fibonacci)
companies.what: Kentucky factory converting hemp stalks into a hardwood substitute for flooring, lumber and millwork.
companies.signal: Commercial since 2019 with US retail distribution of flooring and boards

companies.name: Honext
companies.what: Barcelona startup turning recycled paper-mill cellulose sludge into formaldehyde-free interior boards via an enzymatic process.
companies.signal: Commercial plant in Barcelona; panels specified in European interior fit-outs

variations.white_space: Distribution is the moat, not chemistry: gypsum and OSB incumbents (USG, Knauf, Saint-Gobain, LP) own contractor channels and price points, so bio-boards historically die in the 'green premium' boutique niche. Plantd's national-builder offtake model (D.R. Horton) is the template — winning one production homebuilder beats a thousand one-off architect specs.

variations.name: Bio-based and carbon-storing insulation
variations.description: Wood fiber, hemp, cellulose and wool are manufactured into batt, board and blown insulation that matches mineral and foam R-values with a fraction of the embodied carbon, often storing more carbon than production emits.

companies.name: Steico
companies.what: World's largest wood-fibre insulation manufacturer (Germany/Poland), supplying batts, boards and blown fiber across Europe.
companies.signal: Listed German leader at hundreds of millions of euros in revenue; Kingspan acquired a 51% majority stake (announced 2023)

companies.name: Gutex
companies.what: Century-old Black Forest wood-fibre insulation board maker now pushing into North American distribution.
companies.signal: One of Europe's oldest and largest wood-fibre board producers

companies.name: TimberHP (GO Lab)
companies.what: First and only North American wood-fiber insulation plant, a retrofit of the Madison, Maine paper mill producing TimberFill, TimberBatt and TimberBoard.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 Mar 2025 after $30M+ construction overruns; emerged in 77 days (Jun 2025) with bondholders led by BlackRock affiliates converting to equity and ~$29M new financing

companies.name: Hempitecture
companies.what: Idaho manufacturer of HempWool batt insulation and PlantPanel exterior boards, building a second East Coast plant in Tennessee.
companies.signal: $8.4M DOE MESC grant; ~$6M equity crowdfunding (2025); $1.1M NYSERDA grant

companies.name: Havelock Wool
companies.what: Reno, Nevada producer of sheep's-wool batt and blown insulation for homes and vans.
companies.signal: Niche but established US bio-insulation brand with national shipping

companies.name: Greenfiber
companies.what: Largest US manufacturer of recycled-cellulose (paper) insulation, a mature low-embodied-carbon option sold through big-box and contractor channels.
companies.signal: Multiple US plants; decades of volume production

variations.white_space: North American wood-fiber capacity is effectively a one-plant monopoly (TimberHP) versus a dozen mature European mills, and TimberHP's Chapter 11 reflected first-of-a-kind mill-retrofit cost risk rather than demand risk — products kept selling through bankruptcy. The opening: second and third NA plants sited on existing sawmill residue streams, financed with project debt rather than venture equity, plus straw/hemp lines feeding code-friendly batt formats.

variations.name: Prefab/modular low-energy construction and SIP systems
variations.description: Factory-built panels and volumetric modules — often structural insulated panels or insulated composite skins — compress build schedules and cut both material waste and operational energy through tight, well-insulated envelopes.

companies.name: Vantem
companies.what: Breakthrough Energy Ventures-backed builder of modular homes from high-R insulated structural panels, scaling across the US Southeast.
companies.signal: 2.2M+ sq ft delivered; 325,000+ sq ft/yr capacity; revenue growing yearly

companies.name: Plant Prefab
companies.what: Custom panelized and modular homebuilder (LivingHomes) with the first US factory purpose-designed for hybrid panel/module production.
companies.signal: $30M Series B; 270,000 sq ft Tejon Ranch factory; first B Corp custom modular builder, carbon-neutral operations since 2020

companies.name: Module
companies.what: Pittsburgh startup building net-zero-ready infill housing with panelized/modular methods and a workforce-training 'Last Mile Lab' factory.
companies.signal: Small but operating; city-infill affordable green housing niche

companies.name: Cuby
companies.what: Ships containerized mobile micro-factories that produce a home's complete kit of parts near the job site, selling the factory rather than the house.
companies.signal: ~$6.4M disclosed funding plus factory LOIs; 400,000+ engineering hours; first US deployment (Nevada) targeted 2026

companies.name: Assembly OSM
companies.what: Applies aerospace-style distributed manufacturing (chassis built by existing suppliers) to high-rise modular buildings for NYC.
companies.signal: Raised ~$38M reported (Series A 2022); NYC prototype projects (147 St. Felix); limited public activity recently

companies.name: Bensonwood / Unity Homes
companies.what: New Hampshire pioneer of high-performance timber-frame and panelized shells, prefabricating airtight low-energy envelopes for decades.
companies.signal: 50+ years operating; Unity Homes line productizes near-passive performance

companies.name: Factory OS
companies.what: Union modular factory in Vallejo, CA producing multifamily affordable housing modules at volume for Bay Area projects.
companies.signal: Thousands of units produced; backed by Google, Facebook, Autodesk and Morgan Stanley capital

companies.name: Katerra
companies.what: SoftBank-backed attempt to vertically integrate the entire construction stack from factories to GC services, including a Spokane CLT plant.
companies.signal: Raised >$2B; filed Chapter 11 in June 2021; CLT plant eventually went to Mercer; the sector's canonical failure

companies.name: Veev
companies.what: Panelized 'closed wall' system with HPL skins and integrated MEP for fast-assembly homes.
companies.signal: Raised ~$600M at $1B+ valuation; shut down Nov 2023; Lennar acquired the assets at a steep discount (Dec 2023) and runs it as a subsidiary

variations.white_space: Vertically integrated factory-builders keep dying in housing downturns (Katerra 2021, Veev 2023, Diamond Age 2024): high fixed factory costs collide with cyclical demand and thin construction margins. Surviving models are capital-light — factory-as-product (Cuby), components sold into existing builder channels (Vantem panels), or incumbent-owned offsite capacity (Lennar absorbing Veev) — leaving an opening for component plays that never carry real-estate risk.

variations.name: 3D-printed and robotic construction
variations.description: Gantry and robotic-arm printers extrude mortar walls or assemble structures on-site, cutting labor, waste and schedule; the carbon benefit hinges on low-cement printable mixes since printed walls are otherwise concrete-heavy.

companies.name: ICON
companies.what: Austin leader in 3D-printed homes (Vulcan printers, 100-home Wolf Ranch community with Lennar) plus CarbonX, its lower-carbon printable concrete shipping since April 2024, and the multi-story Phoenix printer.
companies.signal: Raised ~$450M+ at ~$2B valuation (2022); cut ~25% of staff (114 people) in Jan 2025 to refocus on Phoenix and CarbonX

companies.name: Alquist 3D
companies.what: Greeley, Colorado printer of commercial structures; printed Walmart store expansions and now leads the largest US commercial 3D-printing rollout with a printer-leasing ecosystem (FMGI, Hugg & Hall).
companies.signal: Dec 2025 Walmart deal for 12+ retail projects nationwide; third Walmart project underway in Lamar, MO

companies.name: Mighty Buildings
companies.what: Oakland maker of 3D-printed polymer-composite panelized homes marketed on sustainability and fire resistance.
companies.signal: Raised ~$150M; layoffs and a managed sale process in Jan-Feb 2025; technology acquired by Lumus Inc., which continues the product line

companies.name: Diamond Age
companies.what: Phoenix robotics startup that 3D-printed ~30 production homes with Century Communities, then pivoted to light-gauge-steel panels.
companies.signal: Raised ~$58M (Prologis Ventures, Alpaca VC); ceased operations Dec 12, 2024 and entered bankruptcy; equipment auctioned

companies.name: COBOD
companies.what: Danish OEM of the BOD2/BOD3 gantry printers, the largest installed base of construction printers worldwide — a picks-and-shovels play.
companies.signal: Printers deployed in 50+ countries; strategic investors include CEMEX, Holcim, PERI and GE

companies.name: Black Buffalo 3D
companies.what: US/Korean (HN Inc.-backed) maker of NEXCON construction printers and proprietary printable ink targeting multi-story structures.
companies.signal: Commercial printer sales in North America; backed by Korean conglomerate HN Inc.

companies.name: WASP
companies.what: Italian printer maker specializing in raw-earth and natural-material printing (TECLA habitat), the lowest-carbon end of 3DCP.
companies.signal: Crane WASP printers sold globally for earthen construction research and builds

companies.name: SQ4D
companies.what: Long Island company whose ARCS gantry printed some of the first permitted, sold 3D-printed homes in the US.
companies.signal: Multiple permitted homes sold in New York since 2021

variations.white_space: Single-family economics remain unproven — printing replaces one trade among thirty, and two capex-heavy players failed in 18 months (Diamond Age, Mighty Buildings). The defensible openings are commercial/retail printing where schedule is the value (Alquist-Walmart), printer-as-product OEM models (COBOD), and genuinely low-cement printable mixes, since the material — not the robot — is the carbon story.

variations.name: Passive-house components and certified high-performance assemblies
variations.description: Certified windows, heat-recovery ventilators, airtightness membranes, thermal-break connectors and panelized assemblies let builders hit Passive House (PHI/Phius) performance, cutting heating/cooling energy 40-90% at the component level.

companies.name: Zehnder
companies.what: Swiss group whose ComfoAir HRV/ERV units are the de facto ventilation standard in passive-house projects worldwide.
companies.signal: Listed Swiss company; dominant share of certified PH ventilation

companies.name: SIGA
companies.what: Swiss manufacturer of airtightness tapes and membranes used to hit sub-0.6 ACH blower-door targets.
companies.signal: Global distribution; core airtightness brand in high-performance construction

companies.name: Pro Clima (Moll)
companies.what: German maker of Intello smart vapor-control membranes and airtightness systems.
companies.signal: Decades-old category leader sold through PH supply chains worldwide

companies.name: Schöck
companies.what: German manufacturer of Isokorb structural thermal breaks that stop balcony and slab thermal bridging.
companies.signal: Standard specification in low-energy concrete/steel buildings across Europe and NA

companies.name: Alpen High Performance Products
companies.what: Colorado maker of thin-glass, suspended-film high-R windows (up to ~R-14) manufactured in the US.
companies.signal: DOE-supported window technology; expanded Colorado factory to meet demand

companies.name: Zola Windows
companies.what: Colorado-based supplier of Passive House-certified European-style triple-glazed windows and doors for the NA market.
companies.signal: Specified across high-profile US passive house projects

companies.name: 475 High Performance Building Supply
companies.what: US distributor and educator that built the supply channel for PH components (membranes, tapes, wood-fiber insulation) for North American builders.
companies.signal: Key NA channel for European PH products; extensive builder education platform

companies.name: Ecocor
companies.what: Maine manufacturer of certified panelized passive-house wall and roof assemblies shipped as complete shells.
companies.signal: One of the first PHI-certified panelized systems made in North America

variations.name: Embodied-carbon measurement, EPDs and low-carbon procurement software
variations.description: Software calculates whole-building and product-level carbon (LCA/EPDs), benchmarks materials and plugs into design and procurement workflows so teams can specify lower-carbon options — increasingly mandated by Buy Clean policies, CALGreen and EU rules.

companies.name: One Click LCA
companies.what: Helsinki-based market leader in construction LCA and EPD software covering design, procurement and manufacturer workflows.
companies.signal: EUR 40M growth investment from PSG and InfraVia (Nov 2023); customers in 150+ countries incl. Skanska, AECOM, WSP

companies.name: Building Transparency (EC3)
companies.what: Nonprofit steward of the free EC3 tool and openEPD database, the de facto standard for comparing material carbon in Buy Clean procurement.
companies.signal: EC3 embedded in major owner/GC procurement (Microsoft, federal Buy Clean ecosystem)

companies.name: cove.tool
companies.what: Atlanta platform automating building performance, cost and carbon analysis for architects and engineers.
companies.signal: ~$36M raised incl. $30M Series B led by Coatue (2022)

companies.name: Tangible
companies.what: San Francisco platform giving developers and lenders portfolio-level embodied-carbon measurement and material procurement recommendations.
companies.signal: $3M round co-led by Prologis Ventures and Pi Labs (Jan 2025)

companies.name: Preoptima
companies.what: London startup generating whole-life-carbon assessments in minutes at concept stage, before geometry is fixed — when reduction leverage is highest.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; active product and policy content through 2025 (e.g., CALGreen WLC tooling)

companies.name: 2050 Materials
companies.what: API-first platform aggregating and normalizing EPD and product sustainability data for developers and software integrations.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; growing dataset of construction product EPDs

companies.name: Sphera
companies.what: Enterprise LCA software and data house (GaBi datasets) used by manufacturers to produce EPDs at industrial scale.
companies.signal: Blackstone-owned ESG software major; thousands of enterprise customers

companies.name: Autodesk
companies.what: Embeds embodied-carbon analysis into mainstream BIM workflows (Forma, Insight, Revit) with EC3 integration, mainstreaming carbon checks for millions of AEC users.
companies.signal: Dominant AEC software vendor; carbon features shipped across Forma/Insight

variations.name: Deconstruction, material reuse and circular-construction marketplaces
variations.description: Platforms, robotics and reverse-logistics services recover materials (lumber, steel, fixtures, furniture) from demolition and surplus inventory and route them back into projects, displacing virgin-material emissions and landfill.

companies.name: Rheaply
companies.what: Chicago enterprise and citywide reuse exchange that lets organizations list, find and redistribute surplus assets and building materials.
companies.signal: ~$34M raised; 158,000+ asset exchanges in 2024 across new city marketplaces (Seattle, Atlanta, Texas); headcount roughly halved from peak

companies.name: Cambium
companies.what: Traceability software plus 'Carbon Smart Wood' supply chain that turns fallen/salvaged urban trees into tracked lumber, including the first CLT made from salvaged wood.
companies.signal: $18.5M Series A led by VoLo Earth (Feb 2025), $28.5M total; 240+ supply partners; customers incl. Amazon, CBRE, Gensler

companies.name: Urban Machine
companies.what: Oakland robotics startup whose AI-guided machine pulls nails and fasteners from construction/demolition lumber to resell it as premium reclaimed stock.
companies.signal: $14M raised Jul 2025 after $5.6M seed (Lowercarbon Capital, GV, Dec 2022)

companies.name: Madaster
companies.what: Dutch material-passport registry documenting what's in buildings so components can be recovered, financed and reused (EU taxonomy-aligned).
companies.signal: Operating across multiple European countries with institutional real-estate users

companies.name: Concular
companies.what: German circular-construction platform doing pre-demolition audits, material matching into new projects and reuse ESG documentation.
companies.signal: Venture-backed; leading German-market circularity platform with major demolition/developer pilots

companies.name: Globechain
companies.what: UK/US reuse marketplace where enterprises redistribute surplus construction materials, fixtures and equipment with ESG impact data.
companies.signal: 10,000+ member network across UK, US, Spain

variations.white_space: Economics, not technology, keeps this thin: salvage labor costs more than cheap virgin material in most markets, and reclaimed structural members lack easy re-certification, so the sector leans on mandates (EU taxonomy, Portland-style deconstruction ordinances). Openings: robotic processing that collapses labor cost (Urban Machine's wedge), salvage-to-engineered-product upgrading (Cambium's salvaged-wood CLT), and material passports positioned ahead of EU enforcement deadlines.
